entries.en: The beacon.
A vision.
They weren't wasted.
Deal with it!
I just want to stop Saren.
It hasn't been easy.
It's still not clear.
It takes time.
It helped a bit.
You can still help us.
So what good are you?
Welcome aboard.
You can come.
I have spent most of my adult life investigating the Prothean extinction. Decades of intense academic study and field research. And for what?
Yes. Of course. You are right. We need to stop Saren. Commander, I would like to try something. With your permission, of course.
I-- I am sorry, Commander. I don't know what came over me. You are right, of course. We have to stop Saren. That is all that really matters.
You said you have visions. From the beacon. Let me join my consciousness to yours. Maybe my knowledge of the Protheans can help clarify this vision.
Like the asari who gave you the Cipher, I can join my consciousness to yours. Maybe my knowledge of the Protheans will help clarify your vision.
That was incredible! All this time. All my research. Yet I-- I never dreamed... I am sorry. The images were so vivid. I never imagined the experience would be so... intense.
You are remarkably strong-willed, Commander. What you have been through, what you have seen, would have destroyed a lesser mind.
Come on. Get to the point. What'd you see?
The beacon on Eden Prime must have been badly damaged. Large parts of the vision are missing. The data transferred into the commander's mind is incomplete.
Everything I saw you already know. You were right about the Reapers. The Protheans were destroyed by a race of sentient machines.
I think it is obvious there is a connection between the Reapers, the Prothean extinction, and the Conduit. But I did not see anything that would help us find it.
Quite the opposite, Commander. I think my knowledge of the Protheans will prove useful before this is over.
Saren knew you were touched by the beacon on Eden Prime. He probably came after me because he feared I could help you understand it.
I was able to interpret the data relayed through your vision. What was there, at least. Find the missing portion and I'm confident I can put all the pieces together.
You've been through a lot. Dr. Chakwas should take a look at you.
You need food. And sleep. You asari aren't as hardy as my people. You need to see the ship's doctor.
Make it fast. Time's a-wasting.
Do it. Hurry. We don't have much time.
Nobody's messing with my head any more! I'm sick of dealing with these visions!
You sure you didn't come across any kind of clue or hint? Something we might have missed?
Looks like we're back where we started.
What's our next move?
I don't have a choice.
Worth a shot.
So there was nothing useful?
This was pointless.
Try to relax, Commander. Let your mind be swept up in the currents that join us, one to another... embrace eternity.
It's a distress call. A message sent out across the Prothean Empire. A warning against the Reapers. But the warning came too late.
The relay's in the Terminus Systems. They're not fond of Alliance ships over there. Or Spectres.
Saren will have his whole fleet in orbit around Ilos. You will never make it down to the surface without reinforcements.
The Conduit's on Ilos. That's where Saren is heading. I plan to be waiting when he gets there!
Hurry up.
You need to alert the Council. They will assemble a fleet to accompany you. Together you can-- you... ohh. I am feeling a little faint all of a sudden.
They were wiped out by the Reapers, a race of sentient machines.
You wasted your time.
I already know.
Ilos? Never heard of it.
I've never heard of a world called Ilos.
I'm not surprised. Ilos is in a region of space accessible only through the Mu Relay. But the Mu Relay was lost thousands of years ago. Nobody knows where it is.
I recognize some of the landmarks from the photos and vids I had seen during my research. I know of Ilos. I just don't know where it is.
You do? But how... never mind. If you take us to the Mu Relay I can give the vectors to take us to Ilos.
I am afraid so. Unless you find the coordinates for the Mu Relay somehow. Then it would be possible to-- ohh. I suddenly feel a bit faint.
Try to relax, Commander. Let your mind be swept up in the currents that join us, one to another... embrace eternity!
Mission reports are filed, Commander. You want me to patch you through to the Council?
Setting up the link now, Commander.
Aye, aye, ma'am.
Aye, aye, sir.
I have the coordinates for the Mu Relay.
She said it would help me understand my visions. But they still don't make sense.
Patch them through, Joker.
We're in a hurry here.
I can help you.
I saw it!
How'd you learn about Ilos?
Ilos.
I do.
Want me to tell you?
It didn't.
Great. Another alien.
We're done.
You're wasting your time.
I'm not familiar with that world.
Commander. I hope you plan to be civil this time. I don't enjoy getting cut off mid-conversation.
We did. I understand Dr. T'Soni is on the Normandy now.
We've received your report, Commander. I understand Dr. T'Soni is on the Normandy.
I assume you're taking the necessary security precautions?
You are free to act as you see fit, Commander. Our role is to offer guidance and advice.
It's up to you if you're smart enough to listen.
Communications cut, Commander.
Benezia would never allow Saren to kill her daughter.
Maybe she doesn't know.
Or maybe we don't know her. We never expected she could become a traitor.
Matriarch Benezia would never have allowed this if she were still alive. She would have protected her daughter.
Maybe we didn't know her as well as we thought. We never imagined she could be a traitor.
At least the mission was a success.
Apart from the utter destruction of a major Prothean ruin. Was that really necessary, Shepard?
Of course, Commander. The mission must always take priority.
Good luck, Commander. Remember: we're all counting on you.
It won't happen again, Councilor.
You've had a chance to look over the files?
Don't tell me how to do my job!
Sorry, Councilor.
I don't need this.
Liara's on our side. The geth were trying to kill her.
The geth were crawling all over those ruins. We were lucky to make it out alive.
We almost died in there! The geth were everywhere!
Sorry about that.
You saw our report?
She wants to help us.
I know what I'm doing.
That's not necessary.
I apologize.
Disconnect
Dr. T'Soni wants to help.
It was.
I don't care about the ruins!
Miss Williams, Commander - we need to talk. If we do not resolve this situation now, I am afraid things might become... awkward.
Oh, "awkward", huh?
I think we must.
I am afraid it was inevitable.
I disagree.
Jealous? Of you? You're not even our species!
Perhaps that is why you feel threatened. I am a rival unlike any you have faced before. Hostility is a common reaction to the unfamiliar.
Doctor, you keep smart-assing me, I'll show you what my hostile reaction is like.
I agree, Shepard. Which is why you must choose. Ashley or me.
Sorry, Commander. That fantasy's not going to happen.
We're not married, Shepard. You want to get involved with some alien, go ahead. It's none of my business.
Yeah? Kind of hard to feel special while you're always "chatting" with your little blue friend on the side. Or is that my role?
This is exactly what I was trying to avoid. I never should have told you of my feelings, Shepard. I have put you in a terrible position. I am sorry.
I've heard enough. We're resolving this now, Shepard. Me or her?
I understand, Commander. Perhaps it is for the best; she is one of your own kind. I am sure you and Miss Williams will be very happy.
I should... go. I need to... check on something.
Dear God. I think I actually feel sorry for her.
I'm betting you never had your heart broken at fifteen. Rejection hurts, Shepard. Even if you act strong.
Hey. We're all grown-ups here. Right?
In your dreams, Commander.
I hope you two--or however many you end up with--will be happy together.
I hope we can keep this civilized. I do not want things to become... unpleasant.
Because it's been so pleasant between us lately. Look. Somebody in this room needs to make a choice. It ain't me, and it ain't you.
I feel bad for her, Shepard. I hope she'll be okay.
I suppose you're right. I'm sorry you were put in this position, but... I'm glad you chose me.
This is a rather awkward situation.
I'm not trying to make anyone uncomfortable. I'm just trying to figure out where I stand.
I am afraid it was inevitable.
I'm not jealous. I'm confused. I thought we had something, ma'am. I-- I didn't realize you were a-- Well, that you prefer other women.
I am not exactly a woman, Lieutenant. My species only has one gender.
Yeah, but you look-- All right. Shepard, make a choice. If you're not serious about me-- It'll hurt, but I'll get over it. But until you tell me, I can't get over it.
What about Liara? Is she "special," too?
Stop. You can't keep dancing around this, Shepard. Make a choice. Her or me.
I understand, Commander. Perhaps it is for the best; he is one of your own kind. I am sure you and Kaidan will be very happy.
I should go. I need to... check on something.
I can't help but feel a little sorry for her.
Rejection hurts the strong as much as it hurts the weak. I'm glad you're still here, Shepard.
I'll be fine, Commander. We're just friends. I understand.
No. Sorry, Shepard. I mean, if I'd known-- Well. Maybe we just aren't right for each other.
I hope things work out for you two.
I've got a lot of work to do, Commander. Mission reports. That kind of thing. You know how it is.
